items.title: Rotate and revoke JWT refresh-token families
items.objective: Determine whether old refresh tokens mint parallel descendants after rotation, logout, password change, or reuse detection.
prerequisites: A JWT issued to a designated disposable test identity
A harmless identity or authorization endpoint and permission to submit modified tokens
steps: Decode the test token locally and record header, claims, issuer, audience, purpose, key identifier, and lifetime with values redacted
Establish a valid control and one invalid-signature control
Change only the algorithm, key source, claim, time, token type, or lifecycle condition under test
Confirm accepted or rejected server identity/authority and revoke all test tokens

examples.note: Use only synthetic identities and fully redact compact JWT values; decoding is not signature verification.

items.manipulate: One JOSE header, signature/key condition, registered/private claim, token purpose, replay, or lifecycle event at a time
items.secure_behavior: The service verifies signature/MAC with configured trusted keys and algorithms, then validates issuer, audience, type, purpose, time, identity, and current authorization before use.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a consumed or revoked refresh token mints a new access token contrary to lifecycle policy
items.validation: Prove a security-relevant server decision at a harmless endpoint; local decoding, response differences, or an echoed claim alone are insufficient.
false_positives: a tiny retry grace window can intentionally tolerate one near-simultaneous client retry
some refresh tokens are opaque reference tokens rather than JWTs
items.impact: A confirmed JWT weakness can permit token forgery, identity impersonation, privilege escalation, cross-service confusion, replay, or prolonged session compromise.
evidence: Original and modified JOSE header/claims with complete compact tokens redacted
Valid and invalid signature controls
Issuer, audience, purpose, key, time, and test-identity context
Server-side identity/authorization result and revocation cleanup
